description: We are team of students from Ukraine. We love taking on new challenges and working in team. Our team is highly proactive, feels comfortable competing against adults, and is here to win. Unfortunately, our country is at war — many people have lost their sight or suffered other disabilities because of it — and we understand how important it is to promote accessibility in society and in science. Our main goal is to give people with disabilities access to scientific information.
summary:
EchoSphear is an innovative web platform that allows users to experience NASA’s EIC astronomical and climate visualizations through real-time sonification. The site features a curated selection of pre-loaded satellite observations alongside tools to upload and analyze custom photo and video materials with voice- or text-based theme selection. A computer vision algorithm automatically isolates the region of interest within each frame and evaluates color dynamics, scale of change, contrast, and spatial anomalies, translating these graphical parameters into a unique, multi-layered musical composition synchronized with the video feed for simultaneous analysis.

Designed for full accessibility, the project provides an alternative way to perceive scientific data for blind and visually impaired users through complete screen reader support, keyboard shortcuts, an automated voice introduction, an interactive audio legend, and a keyboard-driven step-by-step map exploration mode with spoken readout of coordinates and data values at every point. A consistent sonic grammar - incorporating a reference drone tone, time ticks, spatial stereo panning, and audio event markers — enables accurate auditory interpretation of the scale, temperature, and overall nature of a phenomenon. Users can also select the musical style (from symphony orchestra and choir to piano, ambient, or electronic), independently solo or mute each of the ten instrumental tracks, and save the final output in .WAV format.
details:
EchoSphear is an interactive data sonification web service that transforms NASA satellite visualizations or uploaded photos and videos into musical compositions. Thanks to a unified "grammar of sound," metrics on the map are transformed into pitch, tempo, volume, and panning, allowing climatic and geographical phenomena to be perceived by ear. The project is designed with a focus on accessibility for blind people and includes voice prompts, an audio legend, screen reader support, and tools for interactive map exploration using the keyboard.

Our Github (project):

https://github.com/YehorHres/earth-jukebox

Operating Principle:

After uploading a video or photo material, an algorithm-driven system analyzes and describes what is depicted in the visualization to improve system comprehension and create musical compositions. The next step is splitting the visualization into frames to analyze each one in order to determine graphical characteristics and subsequently convert the corresponding values into musical data. In addition, the system analyzes individual sections of the uploaded material to optimize the identification of context and changes, which enables the algorithm to understand the overall mood and tempo of the composition. As a result, the collected data is converted into a list of musical criteria for each frame to create the final sonified visualization.

Advantages of EchoSphear:

  • Ability to upload both your own photo and video materials and use materials from the library.
  • The site is optimized for use by people with visual impairments, enabling the use of a screen reader and voiceover for all information on the site.
  • Instant music synthesis during playback.
  • Wide variety of settings for the musical composition.
  • Using the "Explore Map" button, you can hear changes in specific areas of the visualization in real time.
  • Downloading the generated composition in .WAV format.
  • Audio legend for a better understanding of the musical interpretation of the piece.

Expected Impact:

EchoSphear ensures equal access to scientific information, allowing blind and visually impaired people to independently analyze NASA satellite maps and understand climatic phenomena by ear. Furthermore, the service raises environmental awareness and expands educational opportunities by transforming complex geographical metrics into understandable and emotionally tangible musical compositions.

Development Tools and Tech Stack:

Frontend: HTML5, CSS3 (custom styles, no frameworks), JavaScript (ES modules, no third-party libraries or bundlers).

Hosting: static site on GitHub Pages without a backend; video analysis and music generation take place entirely in the user's browser, allowing the application to work offline as well.

Visualization Analysis: custom computer vision algorithms built on HTML5 Video, Canvas 2D, and Web Workers — ~25 frame features across 128 zones (color, brightness, Sobel edges, entropy, K-Means clusters), data region detection, color scale extraction (PCA in Lab color space), and motion type classification (globe rotation, camera movement, charts).

Sonification: custom algorithmic composer on Web Audio API (modes, harmony, melody following voice-leading rules, rhythm, track structure), open "data → music" mapping table in JSON, mastering with loudness normalization according to ITU-R BS.1770; instrument samples from tonejs-instruments (CC-BY 3.0) and synthesized timbres.

Accessibility: WAI-ARIA and aria-live for screen readers (NVDA, VoiceOver), full keyboard navigation, Web Speech API for voice topic input and text-to-speech (Ukrainian and English), Vibration API on mobile devices; targeting WCAG 2.2 AA.

Data: visualizations from NASA Scientific Visualization Studio / Earth Information Center (ECCO2, Suomi NPP VIIRS, TROPICS, OCO-2, GEDI, ISS LIS, DYAMOND, etc.).

Testing: ~160 automated browser checks, "golden" track reproducibility tests, audio report (LUFS, peaks, frequency balance), field tests on real EIC videos.

Development Tools: Git and GitHub (repository, branches, pull requests, branch protection rules), GitHub Pages (hosting), Python (local development server only), JetBrains PyCharm (code editor), Google Chrome (testing; DevTools for debugging), custom in-browser tools we built for the project (automated test suite test.html, audio loudness report, “golden” reproducibility tests, field-test tool for real NASA videos, precompute tool for gallery analyses), Claude Code (Claude Opus and Claude Fable models) as an AI coding assistant, Claude (chat) for planning and architecture discussions, Google Gemini for the initial brainstorm of sonification ideas, Google Docs for team feedback; the application itself does not use any AI models at runtime.

Creativity of Our Project:

The creativity of EchoSphear lies in its unconventional combination of science, art, and inclusive design: instead of dry charts, NASA satellite data or the user's own files are transformed into full-fledged music using a unified "grammar of sound." The ability to switch genres (from orchestra to ambient), tactilely explore the map via keyboard with voice guidance, and export tracks in WAV turns the web service into a unique multisensory tool for perceiving Earth by ear.

As a result, we have built a finished website, EchoSphear, capable of transforming science and improving the lives of many people.
